newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria frees two journalists from detention.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria frees two journalists from detention.

text.p: Nigerian has freed two journalists detained without charge, leaving a third still in jail without trial, an opposition newspaper reported on Wednesday.
Freelance journalist Ladi Olorunyomi, detained since March, returned home to her two children last night, the PM News reported on Wednesday.
Also freed was Godwin Agbroko, editor of The Week magazine, who had been detained since December when his magazine published reports about disagreements within the ruling military government.

Journalists groups have recently stepped up their campaign against the detentions. The security authorities normally decline to comment on such issues and there was no independent confirmation of the release.
A third journalist, George Mbah of the independent Vanguard newspaper, remains in detention without trial after arrest last year.

Olorunyomi's husband Dapo Olorunyomi, an editor of the opposition magazine The News, a sister publication of PM News, fled to the United States fearing arrest over reports in the magazine about a coup plot to topple the military government.

Another editor of the magazine is serving a long jail term with three other journalists over the alleged coup plot along with more than 30 former officers including retired General Olusegun Obasanjo, a former military ruler.
Nigeria's military government is under criticism at home and abroad over detentions without trial and the slow pace of its plan to return Africa's most populous nation to democracy.
